title: R' Yehudah the Circumciser
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Shabbat 130b and Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 18:1, R' Hoshaya says, “I asked R' Yehudah the Circumciser,” etc.; Rashi explains that he was a mohel. Hyman understands this Hoshaya to be R' Oshaya, R' Chiya’s student, which would place Yehudah among the last Tannaim, after Rabbi. The supplied notice then breaks off: “and there is…”

notes.text: The supplied Hebrew actually stops after ויש; the sentence is not completed by conjecture. The printed Jerusalem Talmud chapter18 citation is retained as a separate locator question. Hoshaya and Oshaya are both supplied spellings.

The supplied notice genuinely ends at ויש; no continuation is invented. JerusalemTalmudShabbat18:1 remains the supplied citation, while a chapter19 lead is unverified and not substituted. Rashi’s mohel gloss, identification of Hoshaya with Oshaya the student of Chiyya, and the resulting late-Tanna dating remain Hyman’s argument, not newly checked primary claims. Hoshaya/Oshaya remain separate supplied spellings; the title Rabbi alone after whom the Tannaim are dated is kept as Rabbi rather than a newly inserted full personal name.

Hyman’s printed notice cites Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 18:1 and breaks off after “and there is.” The matching exchange in the consulted Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 19:1 has R’ Hoshaya say “we asked” and “he told us,” in a discussion of a dead-end alley. The consulted Shabbat 130b has R’ Oshaya say “I asked” and “he told me,” and Rashi explains that Yehudah circumcised infants. The identification of Hoshaya with Chiya’s student and the resulting date are Hyman’s inferences.
